correctness.rationale: Exact conjugacy to mean/difference equations, strict concavity, hyperbolic-tangent inequality and a continuous endpoint secant quotient prove the global equilibrium threshold and the universal asymmetric biomass deficit. An analytic implicit-function reduction has cubic coefficient beta>0, and Jacobian perturbation proves local attraction. Exact extinction Perron eigenvalue T is parameter-independent. The packaged checker supports, rather than substitutes for, the infinite proof; boundaries, nonlinear critical behavior and global basins are expressly excluded.

value.rationale: A natural two identical-population-patch model, with everywhere-positive redistribution and survival loss, exhibits a provable global sharp threshold for symmetry breaking, two locally stable spatially unequal states, and an all-equilibrium strict loss of total biomass while the classical extinction spectral criterion does not change. This distinguishes survival thresholds from population-composition thresholds and supplies a strong test case for density-dependent dispersal models.
